title: The Man Who Sold The Eiffel Tower
description:
In 1925 the con artist Victor Lustig read that Paris was struggling to maintain the Eiffel Tower. He invited scrap-metal dealers to a hotel, posed as a government official and 'sold' the tower for scrap; one dealer paid him around 70,000 francs including a bribe. The dealer was too ashamed to go to the police, so Lustig returned to Paris and tried again before fleeing to the US. Later he even conned Al Capone out of a few thousand dollars. He is known as 'the man who sold the Eiffel Tower twice'.

Source: Wikipedia, 'Victor Lustig'. The sawing, SOLD sign and mini tower are jokes.
